status: Unreviewed root source-application diagnostic; no original or scoped acceptance
source_proof_under_check: Analytic proof of Proposition3.1, specifically positivity in the normal direction at a generic Rees divisor; AppendixA.1 gives a separate algebraic proof.

own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.base: The smooth affine surface with coordinates x,y; ideal a=(x^3,y^2).
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.normalized_blowup_chart: On the blowup chart r=x^3/y^2 with r invertible, the normalization has coordinates s,r, x=s^2 r, y=s^3 r.
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.normalization_verification: s=y/x is in the fraction field and satisfies s^2=x/r. The ring C[s,r,r^(-1)] is finite over the blowup chart ring, has the same fraction field and is normal.
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.differential: dp=[[2sr,s^2],[3s^2r,s^3]], zero on F, including the normal direction.
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.jacobian: det(dp)=-s^4 r; the relative canonical coefficient is4.
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.regularized_potential: log(|x^3|^2+|y^2|^2) pulls back to6 log|s|^2+2 log|r|^2+log(1+|r|^2).
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.residual_current: For any smooth positive base form omega, eta=p*omega+ddc log(1+|r|^2) has a positive tangent restriction to F but zero normal coefficient on F.
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.volume_orders: For standard omega and r away from0, eta^2 has positive leading order |s|^2, whereas p*(omega^2) has order |s|^8. Their ratio has order |s|^6, not |s|^8 times a smooth positive unit.
own_exact_counterexample_to_normal_injec.conclusion: The asserted normal injectivity and the ensuing smooth volume-ratio step do not hold for this actual normalized blowup.

remaining_repair: Check a valid analytic-local replacement for the Rees discrepancy estimate, for example an exact relative Nadel argument. The independent algebraic AppendixA.1 is not silently promoted to every nonprojective analytic setting.
new_Trusiani_Kahler_input: arXiv:2609.31089v1 Proposition4.1 transfers the earlier analytic argument; its precise supporting chain remains under examination.
